title: Save for required near-term goals (1–5 years out)
summary: Down payment, vehicle replacement, wedding, planned career break — anything with a fixed timeline shorter than five years.
detailsHtml:
Vehicle selection by horizon

Money needed in under 12 months: HYSA, money market funds, or T-bills. Money needed in 1–3 years: short-duration Treasury ladder or short-term bond fund. Money needed in 3–5 years: a conservative blend (perhaps 30–40% equities, balance in short/intermediate bonds), accepting some volatility for moderately better expected return. Money needed in 5+ years: this is no longer a "goal saving" decision; it can be invested more aggressively.

I-Bonds as a tactical layer

I-Bonds (Series I Savings Bonds) earn a fixed rate plus an inflation adjustment, with a maximum $10,000 per person per year purchase. They lock for one year, then have a 3-month interest penalty if redeemed within five years. For a 2–5 year goal where inflation hedging matters, they're a useful supplement to a regular HYSA.
